The weather was clearly an issue. We left New Orleans about 23 minutes after the Learjet left Austin. We flew a similar route across South Florida before crossing the Bahamas on our way to Puerto Rico. We passed through the region about 20 minutes before the Learjet crashed.  

Before we took off, our pilot told us there was bad weather ahead and that the crew would adjust our course to avoid it. We turned north, deviating by about 10 nautical miles, then turned back south once we were past the weather. As a result, we had a smooth ride the entire trip.

Zoom in near Miami and you can see the course change.
